To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the systemic administration of a high dose of TNF- α in ILP is feasible and does not cause severe toxicity; the cytokine is rapidly cleared from the blood stream, but a delayed release of IL-6 occurs in the limb.
high dose TNf-α administration in ILP results, after an initial peak, in extremely high levels in the systemic circulation, without irreversible side effects.
the administration of TNF- α during ILP is associated with extremely high systemic levels of bioactive cytokine, without any irreversible side effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of TNF- in ILP, which is a new and effective method of cancer treatment.
the development of a new method for the treatment of locally spreading melanoma and sarcoma of the limb.

the development of a method for the production of a new class of compounds, the so-called “molecular machines”, which are capable of performing mechanical work by exploiting the energy of a thermal gradient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ILP with rHuTNF- α is safe and effective in limb perfusion.
TNF-α is a safe drug for use in isolation perfusion of limb, and the cytokine release syndrome is not a major concern in the clinical use of TNF- α in ILP.
TNF-α is a potent cytokine which is capable of causing systemic effects, even at the dose used in this study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TNF-α is a potent antitumor agent in ILP and that its systemic toxicity is minimal.
TNF-α is safe and effective for ILP and the systemic cytokine release can be minimized by reducing the leakage of perfusate from the isolated limb.

TNF-α is an effective drug for ILP, but the dose should be reduced in order to prevent the leakage towards systemic circulation and the associated side effects, and that IL-6 is a good marker for TNF-α activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high dose TNFa infusion in ILP resulted in extremely high levels in the systemic circulation with no side effects.

high dose TNFA infusion in ILP resulted in extremely high levels in the systemic circulation, without irreversible side effects, and provoked a delayed blood release in large amounts of IL6; there was correlation between leakage from limb during procedure and magnitude of systemic cytokine levels.
ILP with TNF-α can be administered safely in the clinic without causing severe side effects, and that the systemic cytokine levels can be predicted based on the amount of leakage from the limb.
